understanding.emotion: tired of failing and alone with it

week_beats.steady: You hold that no honest effort is ever lost, and that even a little of it carries you forward.
week_beats.act: You try breaking the loop by doing one small thing today, without waiting to feel ready.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
verse.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचअयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः । अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ॥
verse.line: What happens to someone who believes, tries, slips, and doesn't make it to the end?
verse.translation: Arjuna said: One who has faith but does not strive enough, whose mind falls away from yoga before reaching perfection, what end does he come to, Krishna?
verse.why: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

prasang.title: What becomes of one who falls from yoga
prasang.summary: Arjuna fears that one who falls short is lost like a torn cloud. Krishna promises that no one who does good comes to ruin; past effort carries forward and they strive again.
prasang.lesson: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

verse.meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna: what becomes of someone who believes and tries, but slips before reaching the end? Krishna answers that no sincere effort is ever lost. The path does not close behind them. The work they have already done stays with them, and they simply begin again from where they stopped, without starting over.
verse.for_you: You have been building these apps for years. You do not know what is wrong. This verse says that trying and stopping is not the same as failing. The years you have already spent are not wasted. They stay with you.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son Sanjaya, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: सर्वेषां कर्मणां तात फले नित्यमनित्यता / अनित्यमिति जानन्तो न भवन्ति भवन्ति च अथ ये नैव कुर्वन्ति नैव जातु भवन्ति ते / ऐकगुण्यमनीहायामभावः कर्मणां फलम्
verse.line: Every result is uncertain. Some who try succeed and some don't. Those who never try never do.
verse.translation: The result of every action is uncertain. Knowing this, some people act and succeed, some do not. But those who never act never succeed at all.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.for_you: What is real in you cannot be taken or lost; only what changes can be taken, and you are more than what changes.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha on the second gatekeeper: inquiry (vichara).
verse.sanskrit: या विवेकविकासिन्यो मतयो महतामिह । न ता विपदि मज्जन्ति तुम्बकानीव वारिणि ॥
verse.line: A mind opened by clear thinking doesn't sink in hard times. It floats, like a gourd on water.
verse.translation: Minds that have been opened by discernment do not sink in misfortune, just as gourds do not sink in water.
verse.why: Pick one of calm, clear thinking, contentment or good company. Grow it, and the others follow.

prasang.title: The four gatekeepers: calm, inquiry, contentment, good company
prasang.summary: Vasishtha tells Rama that four gatekeepers guard the door to freedom: calm, inquiry, contentment and good company. He gives a chapter to each, then says you only need to start with one, because each one strengthens the others.
prasang.lesson: Pick one of calm, clear thinking, contentment or good company. Grow it, and the others follow.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha speaks to Rama after he has asked about the four gatekeepers that guard the door to freedom. He explains that a mind opened by clear thinking will not sink when misfortune comes. It stays afloat, like a gourd on water. The point is that you only need to begin with one gatekeeper, such as calm or good company, and the rest will strengthen themselves.
verse.for_you: You are holding your work and your children and your parents, and still you are trying to build. That is not nothing. Even a small hold on something steady, like the effort itself, keeps you from sinking. Trust that this much is enough for today.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: पातितोऽपि कराघातैरुत्पतत्येव कन्दुकः । प्रायेण साधुवृत्तनामस्थायिन्यो विपत्तयः ॥
verse.line: A ball knocked down bounces back up. For good people, setbacks rarely last.
verse.translation: A ball struck down by the hand flies right back up. As a rule, the misfortunes of those who live rightly do not last.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.
verse.misuse: Not a promise that suffering is always short, or that people who suffer long did something wrong.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari speaks to the Reader from the section on steadfastness. He says that a ball knocked down by the hand flies right back up. He means that for people who keep going on the right path, setbacks rarely last. A little honest effort carries you forward, even when it hurts. Your apps may not have taken off yet, but the work itself is not lost. It keeps you from sinking.
verse.for_you: You have been building apps for years while carrying work, children, and parents. That is a lot. The setbacks you face are not the end of your effort. Hold onto the steady part of your day. The work itself is what keeps you from sinking right now.

verse.speaker: Hanuman
verse.setting: Having searched all of Lanka without finding Sita, Hanuman fights off despair.
verse.sanskrit: अनिर्वेदः श्रियो मूलमनिर्वेदः परं सुखम्। भूयस्तत्र विचेष्यामि न यत्र विचयः कृतः॥
verse.line: Refusing to lose heart is the root of success. Look again where you have not yet looked.
verse.translation: Not losing heart is the root of success; not losing heart is the highest happiness. I will search again, in the places I have not yet searched.
verse.why: When you have looked everywhere, look again; giving up costs too much.

prasang.title: Hanuman's search and near despair
prasang.summary: Hanuman searches Lanka all night without finding Sita. He is close to despair, weighing what failure will mean for everyone, then tells himself that refusing to lose heart is the root of success, and searches again.
prasang.story_hook: Hanuman had searched every palace in Lanka by moonlight, and she was nowhere.
prasang.lesson: When you have looked everywhere, look again; giving up costs too much.

verse.meaning: Hanuman has searched all of Lanka through the night and cannot find Sita. Despair weighs on him, and he considers what failure will mean for Rama and the others. He refuses to let that despair settle, telling himself that not losing heart is the root of success and the highest happiness. He resolves to search again in the places he has not yet looked.
verse.for_you: You have looked at your apps and your life and found no answers. Today, search again in one small place you have not yet looked. Do not wait to feel ready. Pick one tiny thing and do it.

verse.speaker: Angada
verse.setting: The monkeys searching for Sita are exhausted and failing; young Angada rallies them.
verse.sanskrit: अवश्यं कुर्वतां तस्य दृश्यते कर्मणः फलम्। परं निर्वेदमागम्य नहि नोन्मीलनं क्षमम्॥
verse.line: Keep working and the results will come. Sink into despair and it is hard to get back up.
verse.translation: Those who keep working surely see the fruit of their work. But once you sink into deep despair, you cannot rise again.
verse.why: Missing a deadline feels final; it rarely is.

prasang.title: The missed deadline
prasang.summary: The southern search party loses time in a magic cave and misses Sugriva's deadline. Angada rallies them once, then despairs, fearing punishment and certain he will be blamed. Hanuman reasons with him to return.
prasang.story_hook: They came out of the cave to find that spring had already come, and their deadline had gone.
prasang.lesson: Missing a deadline feels final; it rarely is.

verse.meaning: Angada, the young prince, speaks to the lost monkey search party. They have missed their deadline and are sinking into despair, fearing punishment and blame. Angada tells them that those who keep working will surely see the fruit of their work. But once you sink into deep despair, you cannot rise again.
verse.for_you: You have been waiting for a sign that your apps are worth it, and that waiting has become its own failure. The loop closes only when you move. Pick one tiny piece of the next app and build it for thirty minutes today. Do not wait to feel ready.

story.title: Building the bridge
story.story_hook: The army stood on the shore with no boats, until a quiet monkey said he knew how to build a bridge.
story.summary: Ram waits three days for the ocean to let him pass, then loses patience. The ocean reveals that Nala can build a bridge; Nala admits his skill and the whole army hauls trees and rocks for five days until the bridge reaches Lanka.
story.lesson: Big things get built by many hands, once someone admits they know how.

story.hook_title: Ram's army stood on the shore with no boats, until a quiet monkey spoke up
story.teaser: Ram's army stood on the shore with no boats, until a quiet monkey spoke up
story.for_you: You have been waiting for the ocean to part, but the bridge is built by admitting you know how and hauling one stone today. Your side project does not need a perfect plan. It needs the first small, honest step.

script: You are tired of failing and carrying it alone. You are on the phone a lot, and you are running on empty. You are building apps on the side, and you do not know what is wrong. You keep going, but you feel stuck.
Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him. Arjuna said to Krishna:
अर्जुन उवाचअयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः, अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति.
In plain words: What happens to someone who believes, tries, slips, and doesn't make it to the end?

Krishna says that no one who does good comes to ruin. The work you have already done stays with you. You simply begin again from where you stopped. This is not about starting over. It is about trusting the path you have already walked. This is easier said than done, because doubt makes you feel like you are starting from zero every time.
This verse is for the years you have spent building. Those years are not erased. They stay with you. You do not have to know what is wrong to keep your effort alive.
What if the work you have already done is enough to begin again?

depth.life: You are carrying the weight of years of side projects that have not taken off, and you feel alone with this failure. The days are full with your work, your children, and your parents, and there is no room to breathe or to understand what is happening.
depth.points: The mind that falls away from its goal before reaching it is not lost. The effort you have already made stays with you. It is not wasted, and it does not mean you are a failure.
depth.practice: Sit with the thought that the years you have already spent are not gone.
depth.question: What would it feel like to let the years you have already spent stay with you?
